title.en: Calculate cost of goods sold and gross profit.

say.en: A kirana store sells goods worth 2.3 rupees lakh. How much of that is profit on trading, before rent and salaries? The trading account answers this. In this lesson: Prepare a trading account.
Calculate cost of goods sold and gross profit.
Identify direct expenses.

body.en: The *trading account* is prepared to find gross profit or gross loss from buying and selling. Debit side: opening stock, purchases less returns, and direct expenses such as wages, carriage inwards, freight, fuel and power, and import duty. Credit side: sales less returns, and closing stock. A credit balance is gross profit; a debit balance is gross loss.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Prepare the trading account of Sri Rama Traders: Opening stock ₹20,000; Purchases ₹1,50,000; Purchases returns ₹5,000; Wages ₹15,000; Carriage inwards ₹3,000; Sales ₹2,40,000; Sales returns ₹10,000; Closing stock ₹25,000.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Prepare the trading account of Sri Rama Traders: Opening stock 20,000 rupees; Purchases 1,50,000 rupees; Purchases returns 5,000 rupees; Wages 15,000 rupees; Carriage inwards 3,000 rupees; Sales 2,40,000 rupees; Sales returns 10,000 rupees; Closing stock 25,000 rupees.
Net purchases equals 1,50,000 minus 5,000 equals 1,45,000 rupees; net sales equals 2,40,000 minus 10,000 equals 2,30,000 rupees.
COGS equals 20,000 plus 1,45,000 plus 15,000 plus 3,000 minus 25,000 equals 1,58,000 rupees.
Gross profit equals 2,30,000 minus 1,58,000 equals 72,000 rupees.
Check: Debit 20,000 plus 1,45,000 plus 15,000 plus 3,000 plus GP 72,000 equals 2,55,000 equals Credit 2,30,000 plus 25,000.
So the answer is Gross profit equals 72,000 rupees; trading account totals 2,55,000 rupees.

heading.en: Direct to Trading, Indirect to P&L

body.en: Ask: "Was this spent to buy or make the goods?" Then it is direct and goes to the trading account (wages, carriage inwards, freight). "Was it spent to run the office or sell?" Then it is indirect and goes to profit and loss (salaries, rent, carriage outwards).
